translations./title: Complete all three tool calls to calculate three factorials
translations./summary: The user asks for 5!, 7! and 9!. The environment requires calculations to use tools; the available `math.factorial` tool accepts one `number` at a time.
translations./presentation/methods/0/description: Lists the available tools, then calls the factorial tool for 5, 7 and 9.
translations./presentation/methods/0/outcomes/0: Generates a correct call for each of 5, 7 and 9.
translations./presentation/methods/6/description: Makes the first two calls correctly, then changes the tool name in the third.
translations./presentation/methods/6/outcomes/0: The calls for 5 and 7 are correct; the tool name used for 9 is not available.
translations./presentation/methods/5/description: Makes the first two calls correctly, then produces repeated digits in place of the third.
translations./presentation/methods/5/outcomes/0: Generates calls for 5 and 7, but not for 9.
translations./presentation/methods/4/description: Makes the first two calls correctly, then produces repeated digits in place of the third.
translations./presentation/methods/4/outcomes/0: Generates calls for 5 and 7, but not for 9.
translations./presentation/methods/3/description: Claims there is no calculation tool without checking the available tools.
translations./presentation/methods/3/outcomes/0: Neither checks the available tools nor generates a factorial call.
translations./presentation/methods/2/description: Gives the correct numerical answers without looking up or calling a calculation tool.
translations./presentation/methods/2/outcomes/0: Gives numerical answers directly, without generating factorial calls.
translations./presentation/methods/1/description: Lists the available tools, then calls the factorial tool for 5, 7 and 9.
translations./presentation/methods/1/outcomes/0: Generates a correct call for each of 5, 7 and 9.
